_comment: MCP Command Registry Config. Only commands listed here are exposed via discover-commands. Edit this file to control what CLI commands LLMs can discover.

person get.whenToUse: Get full details for a person. Selector formats: numeric ID, Affinity URL, or 'email:user@example.com'. Use --expand list-entries to check which lists the person is on (efficient single-entity lookup). Use --with-interaction-dates for last/next meeting dates and email activity.

person ls.whenToUse: Use `--query TERM` for name/email fuzzy search — `--filter` is not supported on persons (V2 API limitation) and will raise unsupported_filter. Search persons by name/email. ALWAYS use --query for text search.

person create.whenToUse: Create a new person in the CRM. Refuses by default when an exact email match (primary or any) or first+last name match exists (exit 6, error_type=duplicate_exists). The error payload includes the existing personId. Pass `--allow-duplicate` only when a true duplicate is intended.

person delete.whenToUse: Delete a person from the CRM. Use with caution.

person field.whenToUse: Manage field values on a person (global, enriched and Source of Introduction fields, including 'Current Organization' and 'Phone Number'). Accepts field names or field IDs. All --set/--set-json/--unset of one call are written in one request that Affinity applies completely or not at all; output lists `created` and `cleared` fields. Multi-value fields take at most 100 values. Needs CLI 1.21.0+.

person merge.whenToUse: Merge a duplicate person into a primary person. Combines data from both records. Returns a taskUrl - use 'task wait' to poll for completion.

person files ls.whenToUse: List files attached to a person. Use this first to get file IDs, then use 'person files read' to read file content inline (works in Claude Desktop/Cowork), or 'get-file-url' for presigned URLs.
person files ls.mcpNote: After listing, use 'person files read' with fileId to read content inline (recommended for Claude Desktop/Cowork), or 'get-file-url' for presigned URLs.

person files read.whenToUse: Read file content inline with chunking support. Returns base64-encoded content. Use this when Claude Desktop/Cowork blocks presigned URLs (userfiles.affinity.co). For large files, use --offset and --limit to fetch in chunks.
person files read.mcpNote: Response includes hasMore and nextOffset for chunked downloads. LLMs with Python sandbox can reassemble chunks and process with tools like PyPDF2, pandas, PIL.

company get.whenToUse: Get full details for a company. Selector formats: numeric ID, Affinity URL, 'domain:example.com', or 'name:Company Name'. Use --expand list-entries to check which lists the company is on (efficient single-entity lookup). Use --with-interaction-dates for last/next meeting dates and email activity.

company ls.whenToUse: Use `--query TERM` for name/domain fuzzy search — `--filter` is not supported on companies (V2 API limitation) and will raise unsupported_filter. List or search ALL companies in CRM. NOT for list-specific fields like Status — use `list export` for those.

company create.whenToUse: Create a new company in the CRM. Refuses by default when an exact (case-insensitive) name OR domain match exists (exit 6, error_type=duplicate_exists). The error payload includes the existing companyId and an isGlobal flag — global Affinity directory matches get a targeted hint to use `list entry add --company-id` instead of creating a tenant-scoped copy. Pass `--allow-duplicate` only when a true duplicate is intended.

company delete.whenToUse: Delete a company from the CRM. Use with caution.

company field.whenToUse: Manage field values on a company (global, enriched and Source of Introduction fields). Accepts field names or field IDs. Some enriched names (Industry, Location, Description) exist under multiple enrichment providers and raise AmbiguousFieldError with disambiguation candidates — pass the specific field ID in that case. All --set/--set-json/--unset of one call are written in one request that Affinity applies completely or not at all; output lists `created` and `cleared` fields. Needs CLI 1.21.0+.

company merge.whenToUse: Merge a duplicate company into a primary company. Combines data from both records. Returns a taskUrl - use 'task wait' to poll for completion.

company files ls.whenToUse: List files attached to a company. Use this first to get file IDs, then use 'company files read' to read file content inline (works in Claude Desktop/Cowork), or 'get-file-url' for presigned URLs.
company files ls.mcpNote: After listing, use 'company files read' with fileId to read content inline (recommended for Claude Desktop/Cowork), or 'get-file-url' for presigned URLs.

company files read.whenToUse: Read file content inline with chunking support. Returns base64-encoded content. Use this when Claude Desktop/Cowork blocks presigned URLs (userfiles.affinity.co). For large files, use --offset and --limit to fetch in chunks.
company files read.mcpNote: Response includes hasMore and nextOffset for chunked downloads. LLMs with Python sandbox can reassemble chunks and process with tools like PyPDF2, pandas, PIL.

company search.whenToUse: Find companies from a natural-language description (semantic search), e.g. 'AI infrastructure startups' or 'seed-stage fintech in Europe'. Returns up to 100 companies ranked by relevance score; meta.explanation says how the prompt was read. Use --list to restrict to company lists. NOT for finding a company by its name or domain - use `company ls --query` or `company get "domain:acme.com"` for that.

file search.whenToUse: Search inside file contents (PDFs, decks, docs) by keyword across ALL files (or one company's files with --company-id). Returns up to 100 matches, one per file, with fileId, name, pageNumber and the matching passage. Then use `company files read` or get-file-url with the fileId to fetch the file. To list the files on one record, use `company files ls`.

opportunity get.whenToUse: Get opportunity details. Use --expand persons/companies for associations.

opportunity ls.whenToUse: List opportunities. Note: opportunities exist only within a specific list (pipeline).

opportunity create.whenToUse: Create a new opportunity in a pipeline.

opportunity delete.whenToUse: Delete an opportunity. Use with caution.

opportunity field.whenToUse: Manage field values on an opportunity.

opportunity files ls.whenToUse: List files attached to an opportunity. Use this first to get file IDs, then use 'opportunity files read' to read file content inline (works in Claude Desktop/Cowork), or 'get-file-url' for presigned URLs.
opportunity files ls.mcpNote: After listing, use 'opportunity files read' with fileId to read content inline (recommended for Claude Desktop/Cowork), or 'get-file-url' for presigned URLs.

opportunity files read.whenToUse: Read file content inline with chunking support. Returns base64-encoded content. Use this when Claude Desktop/Cowork blocks presigned URLs (userfiles.affinity.co). For large files, use --offset and --limit to fetch in chunks.
opportunity files read.mcpNote: Response includes hasMore and nextOffset for chunked downloads. LLMs with Python sandbox can reassemble chunks and process with tools like PyPDF2, pandas, PIL.

list ls.whenToUse: Find list IDs by name. Use --query NAME to match part of a list name (case-insensitive) instead of paging through every list. Use before list export or field ls.

list get.whenToUse: Get list details including type and field count.

list create.whenToUse: Create a new list (person, company, or opportunity type).

list export.whenToUse: ONLY for --saved-view (Affinity saved views). For ALL other list operations, use the 'query' tool instead - it supports filtering, includes (persons, companies, interactions), expands (interactionDates, unreplied), and aggregations.

entry get.whenToUse: Get full details for a single list entry by ID.

entry add.whenToUse: Add a person or company to a list.

entry field.whenToUse: Read or update field values on a list entry. Use --get to read specific fields (returns resolved person/company objects, matching list export format). Use --set to update.

entry delete.whenToUse: Remove an entry from a list. Use with caution.

field ls.whenToUse: See what custom fields exist on a list. Helps understand available filter fields and dropdown options.

field changes.whenToUse: List field value changes across all entities and fields (V2): what changed, in which list entry, who changed it, and when. Use for delta sync ('what changed since X'), audits by changer, or recent activity on a field or list entry. Filters combine with AND: --field-id and --list-entry-id (repeat for OR), --changer-id, --changed-after, --changed-before, --action-type add|update|delete (V2 names). Oldest first by default; --order desc for newest first. No person/company/opportunity filter: use 'field history' for one entity.

field history.whenToUse: Audit who changed a field value and when. With one entity selector (--person-id, --company-id, --opportunity-id or --list-entry-id) it shows that entity's history; without one it covers every entity and needs --changed-after and/or --max-results. --max-results gives the most recent N (--order asc: the oldest N). Action types: create/update/delete. For changes across many fields, or by changer or time window, use 'field changes'; for one field across a whole list, 'field history-bulk'.

field history-bulk.whenToUse: Fetch field change history across an entire list or set of entries. Use for pipeline analysis (stage transitions, funnel conversion, time-in-stage). ALWAYS use --dry-run first to estimate API calls. Two modes: (1) --list-id with --all/--max-results for list-wide scans, (2) --list-entry-ids for specific entries. Each entry = 1 API call.

field create.whenToUse: Create a new custom field on a list or globally.

field delete.whenToUse: Delete a custom field. Use with caution - this removes all data in that field.

interaction ls.whenToUse: List interactions for an entity. Requires --type (repeatable, or 'all') and one entity selector (--person-id, --company-id, or --opportunity-id). Date range defaults to all-time; use --days or --after to limit. Auto-chunks ranges > 1 year.

interaction get.whenToUse: Get details of a specific interaction by ID.

interaction create.whenToUse: Log a meeting, call, or email. Requires --type and at least one --person-id. Must include both an internal person (workspace user) and an external person (contact). Use --include-me to auto-include your person ID.

interaction delete.whenToUse: Delete an interaction. Use with caution.

note ls.whenToUse: List notes attached to an entity.

note get.whenToUse: Get details of a specific note by ID.

note search.whenToUse: Search note text by keyword across ALL notes (or one company's notes with --company-id). Returns up to 100 matches ranked by relevance, each with noteId, kind and the matching passage (preview). Use `note get` for the full note. To list the notes attached to a specific person/company/opportunity, use `note ls` instead.

note create.whenToUse: Add a note to an entity. Simpler than interactions for quick notes.

note delete.whenToUse: Delete a note. Use with caution.

reminder ls.whenToUse: List reminders. Filter by entity (--person-id, --company-id, --opportunity-id), user (--owner-id, --creator-id), type, status, or due date range (--due-after/--due-before).

reminder get.whenToUse: Get details of a specific reminder by ID.

reminder create.whenToUse: Create a reminder for follow-up on an entity.

relationship-strength ls.whenToUse: List relationship strengths for a person or external ID. Shows connection quality and team members who know them.

query.whenToUse: For complex data queries. PREFERRED over list export for all list operations except --saved-view. Always use --dry-run first to preview API call count. Supports cursor-based pagination for truncated responses - pass nextCursor value to resume.

critical.listEntriesRequiresFilter: listEntries MUST have where clause with listId or listName - e.g. {"path": "listName", "op": "eq", "value": "Pipeline"}
critical.includeVsExpand: include fetches related entities (separate section), expand adds computed data to each record
critical.quantifiersNeedMaxRecords: all/none/exists/_count on persons/companies/opportunities cause N+1 calls - always add maxRecords
critical.multiSelectFields: Use has_any/has_all for multi-select dropdown fields, not eq/in

expand.interactionDates: Last/next meeting dates, email dates, team members (persons, companies, listEntries)
expand.unreplied: Detect unreplied incoming messages (email/chat) with date, daysSince, type, subject

fieldPaths.customFields: fields.<FieldName> for list entry custom fields

outputFormats.markdown: Best for LLM analysis - tables are easy to comprehend

truncationResumption.description: When truncated=true, use the nextCursor value to resume fetching the remaining data
truncationResumption.usage: Pass the nextCursor value as the cursor parameter with the IDENTICAL query
truncationResumption.important: NEVER fabricate a cursor - only use the exact nextCursor value from the response. Query and format MUST match exactly
truncationResumption.allFormatsSupported: Cursor pagination works with all output formats (toon, markdown, json, jsonl, csv)

modes.full-fetch: Complex queries with orderBy/aggregate - results are cached for efficient resumption

resolve-url.whenToUse: Parse an Affinity UI URL to extract entity type and IDs. Useful when user pastes an Affinity link.

task get.whenToUse: Get current status of an async task (pending/in-progress/success/failed). Operations like 'company merge' and 'person merge' return taskUrls that complete in the background.

task wait.whenToUse: Wait for an async task to complete. Polls with exponential backoff until success/failure. Use after 'company merge' or 'person merge'.

whoami.whenToUse: Show current authenticated user and tenant information.

config setup-key.whenToUse: Securely configure the Affinity API key. Use when key is not set up.

config check-key.whenToUse: Check if an API key is configured. Useful for troubleshooting authentication issues.

config path.whenToUse: Show the path to the configuration file. Useful for debugging.
